bib.title: Get To The Point: Summarization with Pointer-Generator Networks
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 55th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2017), pages 1073-1083

read.skipped: References skimmed only. No appendix in the PDF; the supplementary material it mentions is not included.

question: Can a seq2seq attentional summariser be made to reproduce facts accurately, handle OOV words, and stop repeating itself on multi-sentence news summaries?
hypothesis: Copying via pointing improves factual accuracy and OOV handling, and a coverage vector with coverage loss removes repetition.
contributions: Hybrid pointer-generator network that can copy source words or generate from the vocabulary
Coverage mechanism (sum of past attention) plus coverage loss to discourage repetition
Result above the previous abstractive state of the art on CNN/Daily Mail by at least 2 ROUGE points

method.summary: Baseline is a single-layer bi-LSTM encoder and LSTM decoder with Bahdanau attention. The pointer-generator mixes the vocabulary distribution and the attention distribution with a learned soft switch p_gen over an extended vocabulary. Coverage is added in a short final training phase.

datasets.name: CNN/Daily Mail (non-anonymized)
datasets.size: 287,226 train / 13,368 val / 11,490 test pairs; articles 781 tokens avg, summaries 3.75 sentences or 56 tokens avg
datasets.source: Hermann et al. 2015; Nallapati et al. 2016
datasets.preprocessing: Original text, no entity anonymization; article truncated to 400 tokens, summary to 100 (train) / 120 (test)

models.name: seq2seq + attention baseline
models.architecture: single-layer bi-LSTM encoder, single-layer LSTM decoder, additive attention

models.name: pointer-generator
models.architecture: baseline + p_gen switch over extended vocabulary

models.name: pointer-generator + coverage
models.architecture: adds coverage vector in attention and coverage loss

training.objective: mean per-step NLL of reference word; coverage phase adds lambda * sum_i min(a_i, c_i), lambda=1
training.optimizer: Adagrad, initial accumulator 0.1, gradient clipping max norm 2
training.steps: baseline about 600,000 iterations; pointer-generator under 230,000; coverage 3000 further
training.regularisation: none; early stopping on validation loss
training.wall_clock: baseline 4 days 14 h (50k), 8 days 21 h (150k); pointer-generator 3 days 4 h; coverage about 2 h

other.optimizer_choice: Adagrad found best of SGD, Adadelta, Momentum, Adam, RMSProp
other.curriculum: start with highly truncated sequences, raise max length once converged
other.coverage_loss_start: coverage loss converged to about 0.2 from about 0.5; lambda=2 reduced coverage loss but raised primary loss, not used

inference.samples: single output per article; single run

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L F1
metrics.definition: word, bigram and longest-common-subsequence overlap with reference, pyrouge 0.1.3

metrics.name: % duplicate / novel n-grams
metrics.definition: share of summary n-grams repeated within the summary or absent from the article

eval.protocol: ROUGE 95% CI at most +/-0.25; METEOR gains tested with approximate randomization p<0.01; one reference summary per article; Nallapati numbers use anonymized data so are not strictly comparable

availability.data: non-anonymized data scripts and model outputs at the same GitHub repository

terms.definition: hybrid between baseline and a pointer network, allowing both copying words via pointing and generating words from a fixed vocabulary
sum of attention distributions over all previous decoder timesteps
soft switch in [0,1] weighting generating from the vocabulary vs copying from the source

code.snippet: P(w) = p_gen P_vocab(w) + (1 - p_gen) sum_{i: w_i = w} a_i^t
p_gen = sigma(w_h*^T h*_t + w_s^T s_t + w_x^T x_t + b_ptr)
loss_t = -log P(w*_t) + lambda sum_i min(a_i^t, c_i^t)
